prompt:
Produce the requested compact final artifact. Use the simplest behavior consistent with the public specification and pick a reasonable convention where it is silent. Keep private deliberation short.
Public specification:
Build a 4-digit BCD (binary-coded decimal) counter. Each decimal digit is encoded using 4 bits: q[3:0] is the ones digit, q[7:4] is the tens digit, etc. For digits [3:1], also output an enable signal indicating when each of the upper three digits should be incremented. Include a synchronous active-high reset.

Treat this document as behavioral evidence. Follow the artifact and interface instructions in this request when the release describes testbench scaffolding or coverage goals.
Public interface: input widths {'reset': 1}; output widths {'ena': 3, 'q': 16}.
Frozen timing: Clock clk; driven input row before the posedge sample, sampled after that edge settles. Optional mid changes inputs after this sample, before the other edge. The next row drives new inputs before the next sample.
Return only executable Python def reference(vectors), with no imports, external state
or executable top-level code. Return exactly one dictionary of concrete unsigned integers per
supplied input row, with every output on every row. Widths must fit. Use concise named state.
Use brief private deliberation. Prioritize the complete artifact before the token limit.
response:
```python
def reference(vectors):
    q = 0
    out = []
    for v in vectors:
        reset = v['reset']
        if reset:
            q = 0
        else:
            ones = q & 0xF
            tens = (q >> 4) & 0xF
            hundreds = (q >> 8) & 0xF
            thousands = (q >> 12) & 0xF
            ones += 1
            if ones == 10:
                ones = 0
                tens += 1
                if tens == 10:
                    tens = 0
                    hundreds += 1
                    if hundreds == 10:
                        hundreds = 0
                        thousands += 1
                        if thousands == 10:
                            thousands = 0
            q = (thousands << 12) | (hundreds << 8) | (tens << 4) | ones

        ones = q & 0xF
        tens = (q >> 4) & 0xF
        hundreds = (q >> 8) & 0xF
        e0 = 1 if ones == 9 else 0
        e1 = 1 if ones == 9 and tens == 9 else 0
        e2 = 1 if ones == 9 and tens == 9 and hundreds == 9 else 0
        ena = (e2 << 2) | (e1 << 1) | e0
        out.append({'q': q, 'ena': ena})
    return out
```
